To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a single-stage, grid-connected, PV system can be controlled in such a way that its dynamics are independent of those of a distribution network, and the PV system does no affect the dynamics of the network.

(1) The proposed control strategy for the PV system decouples the PV dynamics from the network and load dynamics, (2) The PV system dynamics are decoupled and are not influenced by the network dynamics, and (3) The proposed control scheme enables the PV system to maintain its stability and dynamic performance under wide variations of the network dynamics.
the proposed control strategy enables a single-stage, PV system to interface with a distribution network without destabilizing it.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a control strategy and a dynamic model that are suitable for the design of a robust controller for a PV system connected to a distribution system.
the development of a control strategy that enables proper control and maximization (i.e., tracking of the MPPT) of the PV system output.
the development and analysis of a control strategy for the PV system that is connected directly to the distribution network and is capable of providing maximum power to the network.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the proposed control strategy enables decoupled control of the PV system and, therefore, enables the design and optimization the PV system controllers independently of the network and load characteristics.

under the proposed controller design methodology, the PV system is dynamically decoupled from the distribution network, and the PV system can be designed and optimized independently of the distribution network characteristics.
the proposed control strategy and feedforward compensation mechanisms enable the PV system to be operated as a stand-alone system, with the network and the load being transparent to the PV system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a single-stage PV system with a properly designed control strategy is a viable solution for interfacing a distributed PV source with a distribution network.

the proposed control methodology enables the PV system to operate in a stable and robust manner and, thus, facilitates its integration with the distribution network without destabilization or degradation of the power system dynamics and stability.

the proposed control strategy and feedforward compensation mechanisms enable the PV system to operate in a wide range of conditions, without destabilizing the network, and without affecting the PV system dynamic performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the proposed PV system controller is robust and stable, and can be designed to meet performance objectives without compromising robustness and stability of the overall system.
the proposed control methodology can be used to design and optimize controllers for PV systems, to ensure stability and performance, and to characterize the dynamics of the system.
a PV system can be interfaced with a distribution network in a stable manner, and that the PV system does have a stable dynamics that are independent of the dynamics of the distribution network.
